cards.b: Training must match the demands of the activity and the fitness component to improve.
Gradually increasing the workload so the body keeps adapting.
Working harder than normal so the body adapts.
Fitness gained is lost when training stops or reduces.
Boredom from repetitive training, lowering motivation.
Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type: ways to apply overload.
Too much training with too little rest: injury, illness, lower performance.
Continuous running with changes of speed and terrain.
Explosive jumps such as depth jumps and hurdle jumps; improves power.
Series of stations each targeting a fitness component or muscle group.
High-intensity work intervals with rest or low intensity periods; rest removes waste products.
Heaviest weight that can be lifted once; used to set weight training intensity.
Makes more red blood cells, helping endurance; hard to train at normal intensity.

gaps.s: Training that matches the needs of the sport is called ___.
The F in FITT stands for ___.
Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 minus your ___.
Continuous training is done at 60 to 80 per cent of maximum ___ rate.
Losing fitness when training stops is called ___.
Depth jumps are an example of ___ training.
The ___ scale is used to rate how hard you feel you are working in fartlek training.
Training too much without enough rest is called ___.

short.q: Describe how a footballer could apply overload using FITT.
short.model: Increase frequency (e.g. 3 to 4 sessions), intensity (higher heart rate), time (longer sessions) or change type of training.

short.q: Calculate the 60–80% heart-rate zone for a 16-year-old.
Give one advantage and one disadvantage of fartlek training.
short.model: Advantage: varied so less boring, no equipment. Disadvantage: hard to measure intensity, easy to go easy on yourself.

short.q: Explain why a volleyball player would use plyometric training.
short.model: It improves power by training explosive jumps, which helps the player jump higher to spike or block.

short.q: Explain one disadvantage of high-altitude training.
short.model: It is hard to train at normal intensity because there is less oxygen, or the benefits are lost quickly (reversibility).
